name: Tinder
description: Tinder on this phone is the website tinder.com, logged in inside Chrome (com.android.chrome) -- there is no Tinder app installed. Chrome runs in its tablet layout: a tab strip, then a toolbar of Home, 'Go back', 'Go forward', 'Reload this page', the address bar (id=url_bar, e.g. 'tinder.com/app/matches'), 'Translate', 'See 1 tab' and the Chrome menu. Everything below the toolbar is the Tinder page. Its bottom nav, left to right: 'Tinder' (the swipe deck), 'Explore', 'Likes You' (paid), 'Messages', 'My Profile'. All messaging lives on Messages (tinder.com/app/matches): a 'New matches' row of photo tiles above a 'Messages' list of conversations.

workflows.name: open_messages
workflows.steps: open_app com.android.chrome. The Tinder tab is normally still open where it was left; the address bar (id=url_bar) says which page: 'tinder.com/app/matches' is the Messages screen, 'tinder.com/app/messages/<id>' a chat, '.../profile/<id>' a match's profile, 'tinder.com/app/recs' the swipe deck. To reach Messages, tap [Button] 'Messages' in Tinder's bottom nav (fourth from the left, a speech-bubble icon) -- not Chrome's toolbar. Only when no Tinder tab is open at all, open_url https://tinder.com/app/matches (every open_url opens a NEW Chrome tab, so do not use it to switch pages). If the element list shows only Chrome's toolbar and a bare 'Web View', the page has not populated into the accessibility tree yet: wait one turn and look again. The Messages screen reads, top to bottom: the TINDER logo with 'Safety Toolkit' (shield, top-right); 'New matches' above a horizontal row (Scroller, scrollable-h) whose first tile is [Button] 'Get Likes' (id=likes-you, paid -- not a match) followed by one [Button] '<name> <name>' per new match ('<name> <name> Verified!' when they carry the blue verified tick); then 'Messages' above one row per conversation, listed as [Scroller] '<name> Report Unmatch' (scrollable-h).

workflows.name: scan_new_matches
workflows.steps: On the Messages screen, inspect the 'New matches' horizontal row. Skip the first tile 'Get Likes' (paid upsell). A new match is indicated by a small RED DOT on its tile (visible in the screenshot; the element list does not show the dot). The blue verified tick is NOT the dot. Do NOT tap or open any match tile -- opening one marks it seen and permanently clears the dot. Newer matches appear first; swipe the row left (the only safe sideways swipe on Tinder) only while the last tile on screen still has a red dot.

workflows.name: scan_messages_list
workflows.steps: Inspect the conversation rows listed under 'Messages'. CRITICAL SAFETY: Never swipe a conversation row sideways -- swiping sideways slides the row over and reveals red 'Report' and grey 'Unmatch' buttons; unmatching is irreversible. If a row ever slides open, reload the page via Chrome's toolbar to reset it. Scroll the list strictly vertically. An unread incoming message is indicated by a small RED DOT on the right edge of the circular photo (visible in screenshot; not in element list). Read the preview under the name off the screenshot. A preview starting with a curved arrow (↩) is your own outgoing message. Do NOT tap or open any conversation -- opening marks it read and clears the dot.

workflows.name: dismiss_popups_and_sync
workflows.steps: Chrome's own sign-in and sync screens ('Make Chrome your own', 'Sign in to Chrome', 'Continue as <name>', 'Turn on sync'): always select 'Stay signed out', 'No thanks' or 'Use without an account'. Never tap 'Continue as ...' or accept terms. Dismiss Tinder web overlays (Tinder Gold/Platinum upsells, 'Turn on notifications', Chrome's 'Add to Home screen' or Translate prompts) with close X, 'No thanks', 'Maybe later', or 'Not now'.

nuances: Tinder here is a web page, so its elements come from Chrome's accessibility tree. Right after Chrome comes to the front, the element list can show nothing of the page but a bare [Text] 'Web View' under Chrome's toolbar; wait one step and look again -- the page's elements appear once Chrome has filled the tree in.

On the Messages list, the element list gives each conversation only as '<name> Report Unmatch' -- neither the unread red dot nor the message preview is in the element list; read both off the screenshot under the name. A preview that starts with a small curved reply arrow (↩) is YOUR message, i.e. the match has not answered; a preview with no arrow is the match's message.

Each conversation row on the Messages list is a horizontal scroller: swiping it sideways slides the row over and uncovers a red 'Report' button and a grey 'Unmatch' button. Unmatching deletes the match and the whole chat; it cannot be undone. Never swipe a row sideways, and if a row is ever showing Report / Unmatch, do not tap anywhere on that row -- tap a different row, or tap 'Reload this page' in Chrome's toolbar to close it. Scroll the Messages list only vertically.
The 'New matches' row also scrolls sideways (it is a horizontal list of tiles, not a swipe deck): swiping it left shows more new matches. That is the only horizontal swipe that is safe on Tinder.

The 'Tinder' tab in the bottom nav (flame icon, tinder.com/app/recs) is the swipe deck: a swipe or a tap on its heart / X / star buttons likes, passes or Super Likes a profile and cannot be undone. 'Explore' is another browsing surface, 'Likes You' and the 'Get Likes' tile are paid (Tinder Gold), and 'My Profile' is your own profile.
The element list renders emoji as '..' (every character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane becomes two dots): a message reading 'Hey hottie ..' ends in an emoji. Read emoji off the screenshot.

Tinder web may put up overlays -- a Tinder Gold / Platinum upsell, 'Turn on notifications', Chrome's own 'Add to Home screen' or Translate prompts. Dismiss them with their close X, 'No thanks', 'Maybe later' or 'Not now'; never subscribe, purchase or allow notifications.
If the page shows a login screen ('Log in', 'Create account', a phone-number or Google sign-in prompt), the Tinder session has expired. Do not try to log in; stop the pass and say so.
recommendations: Every pass: open_app com.android.chrome, tap 'Messages' in Tinder's bottom nav, and work only on the Messages screen.
Read all new match dots and unread message dots off the screenshot -- never open match tiles or conversations.
Decide which conversations have unread messages by looking for the red dot on their photo and checking the preview text (no ↩ arrow = match's message).
Scroll the Messages list strictly vertically; never swipe a conversation row horizontally.
End the pass on the Messages screen.
